Reference / digest/legacy

digest/legacy#

MD5 (RFC 1321) and SHA-1 (RFC 3174), for legacy interoperability only.

Version: v1.0.0

Synopsis#

let prefix = Md5([byte(97), byte(98)]);
let whole = prefix.state([byte(99)]);
whole.bytes(); // 16 raw bytes for "abc"; display with HexEncoded

Description#

MD5 (RFC 1321) and SHA-1 (RFC 3174), for legacy interoperability only. Neither algorithm may be used for new security decisions: collision resistance is broken. These objects represent byte messages, not passwords or MACs.

Md5()/Sha1() bind empty input; the one-argument constructor binds @byte. Construction performs no compression. bytes() computes 16/20 raw bytes lazily on a temporary finalized state, without changing this receiver. Encode text explicitly (e.g. Utf8Encoded) and format separately (HexEncoded). state(bytes) compresses old full blocks and binds the new chunk unevaluated, retaining only chaining words, a <=63-byte tail, length and the new array. Empty append, branches, repeat observations and append after bytes() are valid. DigestInputTooLong from digest/blocks rejects total length above 2^61-1 bytes. No native digest provider, I/O, mutable cache or owned resource. Work is linear in pending bytes; repeated queries recompute the pending chunk.
